# Reaction-effect matrices and material-transport interval tables

The data below belong to [Theorem L.4.2c](../../../appendices/appendix_l_cc_mechanism.md). Its native proof supplies the spin-chemical source, exact generator, reaction-floor inverse, finite-source tails, spatial transport and complete resource ownership.

<a id="reaction-effect-matrices"></a>
## Rational reaction-effect matrices

Use the theorem's product-$z$ tensor order, with electron labels $(+1/2,-1/2)$, nuclear labels $(1,0,-1)$, and the last tensor factor varying fastest. For $B=9,99/10,101/10,11$ mT,
$$
 \widehat E_B=10^{-14}A_B.
$$
The table specifies the upper triangle of each Hermitian $36\times36$ integer-complex matrix. An entry $(a,b)$ means $a+ib$. Every unlisted upper-triangular entry is zero, and $(A_B)_{ji}=\overline{(A_B)_{ij}}$. Indices start at one. These rules specify all $4\cdot36^2=5184$ matrix entries.

<a id="refined-reaction-coil-ramp-bounds"></a>
## Refined reaction, finite-source and ramp bounds

The following exact rational bounds use the same four $36\times36$ reaction-effect
matrices above and the source, reaction floor, finite-coil geometry and complete-cycle
ledger of [Theorem L.4.2c](../../../appendices/appendix_l_cc_mechanism.md).
The reaction generator has inverse-microsecond units and a reaction floor of one
per microsecond. The candidate yield is $\operatorname{Tr}(\widehat E_BQ_T/27)$.
The residual row-sum bound controls the effect error through the reaction-floor
inverse; each arm's error and finite-source tail is added once to its contrast
interval. The rational comparisons use the theorem's Machin-series and
integer-square-root enclosures. Decimal entries below are approximations, not
replacements for the exact rational endpoints.

For the ramp calculation the currents have the specified compact, divergence-free
closed-wire supports. If $M_1\ge\int |x|\,|J_c^0(x)|\,dx$, the main proof gives
$$
E_{\mathrm{ramp},c}\le
\frac{\mu_0M_1^2}{4\pi c_{\mathrm{light}}^3}
\int |f''(t)|^2\,dt.
$$
For two quintic ramps of duration $\tau_r$ seconds,
$\int|f''|^2=240/(7\tau_r^3)$. The final exact coefficient below therefore
multiplies $\tau_r^{-3}$ and has units joule times seconds cubed. The common
current-moment bound does not identify the branch-dependent radiation or total
drive work; those retain their separate terms in the main proof's energy ledger.
